1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 — the byte-vs-rune lot — were fixed together; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). The remainder is unfixed and reachable from the current code.
16	
17	### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not
18	
19	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`
20	
21	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
22	comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
23	enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.
24	
25	A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
26	grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
27	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.
28	
29	**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
30	or drop the claim from the doc comment.
31	
32	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
33	
34	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
35	
36	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
37	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
38	
39	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
40	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
41	than a drive-by fix.
42	
43	### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`
44	
45	`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`
46	
47	After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
48	`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
49	`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.
50	
51	Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
52	happen and is misleading to read.
53	
54	### D7 — `extractTarGz` keeps parent references in archive paths
55	
56	`internal/oci/oci.go:262`
57	
58	Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
59	member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
60	references.
61	
62	**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
63	`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
64	actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.
65	
66	Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
67	under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
68	`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.
69	
70	**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
71	them.
72	
73	### 1.1 Fixed
74	
75	**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
76	looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
77	fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.
78	
79	Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
80	`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
81	the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
82	terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
83	ones.
84	
85	A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
86	in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
87	Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
88	gone.
89	
90	The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
91	(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
92	`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).
93	
94	One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
95	`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
96	so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
97	theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
98	
99	**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
100	planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.
101	
102	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
103	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
104	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
105	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
106	same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
107	won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
108	after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
109	strips the path before the helper is ever called.
110	
111	**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
112	the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
113	change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
114	`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.
115	
116	Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
117	path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
118	contexts anyway.
119	
120	Two smaller defects went with it:
121	
122	- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
123	  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
124	  hang indefinitely.
125	- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
126	  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
127	  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
128	  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.
129	
130	`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
131	than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
132	`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
133	common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
134	`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
135	`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 2. Technical debt
140	
141	### Test coverage
142	
143	Currently **18.2 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
144	**+7 250 covered statements** over today's ~2 100.
145	
146	Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:
147	
148	| Phase | Scope | Status |
149	|---|---|---|
150	| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
151	| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
152	| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | pending (~1 240 stmts) |
153	| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
154	| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
155	| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
156	| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |
157	
158	Phase 1 progress:
159	
160	| Package | Before | Now |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (new) |
163	| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |
164	| `internal/ui/help` | 0 % | **96.7 %** |
165	| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79.8 %** |
166	| `internal/oci` | 0 % | **33.6 %** |
167	| `internal/docker` | 7.3 % | **65.4 %** (phase 5, pulled forward — see below) |
168	| `internal/gitlab` | 7.5 % | **100 %** |
169	| `internal/credentials` | 29.5 % | **98.2 %** |
170	
171	`internal/oci` stops at 33.6 % because the remaining statements are registry HTTP
172	paths (`DownloadTemplate`, `listCatalog`, `ListTemplates`) that need a fuller
173	`httptest` fixture — a manifest plus a gzipped layer — rather than the
174	single-response stubs used so far.
175	
176	Phase 5's blocker is cleared for `docker`: the package now routes every CLI
177	invocation through the `dockerRunner` seam in `internal/docker/exec.go`, so tests
178	drive argument building and output parsing against canned output. `scan` and
179	`app` remain.
180	
181	`internal/gitlab` needed no seam: every function takes a `*gitlabclient.Client`
182	built from a base URL, so an `httptest` server standing in for the API covers
183	the whole package. `Clone` is exercised against a throwaway local repository
184	rather than mocked, and skips when no `git` binary is on `PATH`.
185	
186	`internal/credentials` needed no seam either. `git credential` is steerable
187	through the environment, so the tests redirect `HOME`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and
188	`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` at a temporary directory and run the real binary against a
189	throwaway `store` helper — nothing reaches the developer's keychain. Running the
190	real git is what surfaced the context-isolation defect recorded in §1.1; a stub
191	would have frozen the broken behaviour instead. The 2 s timeout is covered by
192	installing a credential helper that sleeps.
193	
194	### Files over the 800-line ceiling
195	
196	The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Seven exceed it:
197	
198	| File | Lines |
199	|---|---|
200	| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1785 |
201	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
202	| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
203	| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1214 |
204	| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1133 |
205	| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 995 |
206	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |
207	
208	`internal/docker/client.go` (1176 lines — the 1069 recorded earlier was stale)
209	was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,
210	`volumes.go`, `registry.go`, `launch.go`, `system.go` and `parse.go`; the largest
211	is now 269 lines. The former `network.go` became `ports.go`, since it reports the
212	host's listening sockets via `ss` rather than Docker networks — the name was
213	free for the `docker network` family.
214	
215	This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
216	tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
217	Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
218	7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.
219	
220	### Race detector cannot run locally
221	
222	`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
223	it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
224	concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.
225	
226	**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
227	every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
228	run reported no data race across all 17 packages.
229	
230	That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
231	tests actually execute, and coverage is 18.2 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
232	paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
233	this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.
234	
235	Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
236	avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 3. Planned features
241	
242	Carried over from `todo.md`.
243	
244	### 3.1 Network diagnostics
245	
246	- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
247	  redirections to the host machine.
248	
249	### 3.2 Interactive security remediation
250	
251	- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
252	  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
253	- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
254	  directly into the Workspace view.
255	
256	### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser
257	
258	- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
259	  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
260	  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
261	    the Docker daemon).
262	  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
263	    downloading the whole image.
264	  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
265	  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
266	- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
267	  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".
268	
269	### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers
270	
271	- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
272	  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
273	- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
274	  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.
275	
276	### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)
277	
278	- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
279	  for every container in the selected project.
280	- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).
281	
282	### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context
283	
284	Support GitHub as well as GitLab, with **exactly one backend active per
285	configuration context**. A context targets one forge; switching forge means
286	switching context.
287	
288	Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
289	not a chosen design.
290	
291	#### What is coupled to GitLab today
292	
293	| Surface | Size |
294	|---|---|
295	| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
296	| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |
297	
298	The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
299	(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
300	rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
301	interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.
302	
303	Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
304	clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
305	and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
306	`shared.GitLabStats`.
307	
308	#### Model mismatches to settle before coding
309	
310	These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
311	promise.
312	
313	- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
314	  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
315	  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
316	  backend declares.
317	- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
318	  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
319	  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
320	  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there — see also D2.
321	- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
322	  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
323	  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
324	  limits and semantics.
325	- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
326	  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
327	  applies either way.
328	
329	#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs
330	
331	Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
332	package needs a seam.
333	
334	Arguments for the CLIs:
335	
336	- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
337	  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
338	  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
339	- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
340	  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
341	- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.
342	
343	Arguments against:
344	
345	- **Per-context isolation conflicts with how these tools store auth.** Both keep
346	  global per-host state (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`). DevDesk contexts want
347	  *different tokens for the same host*. Driving `gh auth switch` from the TUI
348	  would mutate the user's global CLI state — the exact mistake avoided in §1.1 by
349	  scoping `credential.useHttpPath` to the invocation. The clean route is
350	  `GH_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` per invocation, but then DevDesk still owns the
351	  tokens and the main benefit is gone.
352	- **Two more hard dependencies.** Today DevDesk needs `git`, and `docker` only
353	  for the features that use it. Requiring `gh` and `glab` for the core forge
354	  feature is a real setup-friction regression.
355	- **Cost per call.** A process spawn per request, against a reused HTTP
356	  connection today. The dashboard alone issues five calls, and the explorer
357	  paginates.
358	- **Testability regresses.** `internal/gitlab` reaches 100 % with no seam,
359	  because the SDK takes a base URL that an `httptest` server can stand in for.
360	  Shelling out would put it back in the position `internal/docker` was in, needing
361	  a manufactured seam — and stubbed CLI output encodes assumptions about the tool
362	  rather than testing against it.
363	
364	**Current recommendation:** keep Go SDKs (go-gitlab, go-github) for the API
365	surface, and use the CLIs only as an *optional* token source — when a context has
366	no token, offer to read one from `gh auth token --hostname <host>` or
367	`glab auth status`. That takes the convenience without the coupling. Recorded as
368	a recommendation, not a decision.
369	
370	#### Sketch of the work
371	
372	1. Define a `forge` abstraction from what the code actually consumes: current
373	   user, namespace tree, create/delete namespace and repository, initial commit,
374	   dashboard counters, clone URL.
375	2. Replace `shared.State.GitLabClient` with that interface. This is the change
376	   the other 65 call sites follow from.
377	3. Generalise `GitLabConfig` into a per-context forge config carrying a
378	   `type: gitlab | github` discriminator, and migrate existing config files.
379	4. Implement the GitLab backend by moving the existing code behind the
380	   interface — behaviour-preserving, and covered by the tests added in #7.
381	5. Implement the GitHub backend.
382	6. Rename the views and commands, keeping `gla` / `gle` as aliases so muscle
383	   memory survives.
384	
385	Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own: they are a refactor of working code with
386	tests already in place, and they are what makes step 5 tractable.
387	
388	---
389	
390	## 4. Existing plans
391	
392	Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is referenced directly from the old
393	`todo.md` and is still outstanding:
394	
395	- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
396	  — Docker-layer platform portability.

Backlog lu (`docs/backlog.md`, à jour au 2026-08-02). État réel vérifié dans le code :

**Défauts ouverts** (D1/D3/D6 et l'isolation des credentials sont faits en #5/#8)

| # | Sujet | Poids |
|---|---|---|
| D7 | `extractTarGz` (`internal/oci/oci.go:262`) garde les `..` dans les clés — Zip Slip latent | petit, sécurité |
| D2 | Checkbox « permanent delete » documentée comme verrouillée mais togglable | petit |
| D5 | Clamp de focus mort dans `CreationForm` | trivial |
| D4 | `Tab` pour naviguer entre champs (viole Rule 135) | nécessite un arbitrage UX |

D7 et D2 ont chacun un test « pinned » qui `t.Skip()` dès que le défaut est corrigé (`internal/oci/oci_test.go:161`, `internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal_test.go:202`) — ils sont conçus pour être remplacés par de vraies assertions.

**Dette technique**
- Couverture : 18,2 % global, cible 80 %. Phase 1 close sauf le complément `ui/theme` (à 81 % aujourd'hui, ~55 stmts restants). Phase 2 = `status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth` (~1 240 stmts).
- 7 fichiers > 800 lignes. Le backlog signale lui-même le conflit d'ordre : écrire des milliers de statements de tests contre `security/model.go` (1785) ou `oci_resources/update.go` (1556) fige leur structure avant le split.

**Features** : multi-forge GitHub (étapes 1–4 = refactor de code testé, faisable seul), port-forwarding, dive-like, etc.

Ma recommandation : une PR courte D7 + D2 + D5 d'abord (auto-contenue, deux tests attendent déjà, D7 est le seul à portée sécurité), puis attaquer la phase 2 de couverture. D4 reste en attente d'une décision de ta part.

53	func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*DeleteConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
54		switch msg := msg.(type) {
55		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
56			m.width = msg.Width
57			m.height = msg.Height
58	
59		case tea.KeyMsg:
60			switch msg.String() {
61			case "up", "k":
62				// Navigate up
63				if m.focused > 0 {
64					m.focused--
65				}
66				return m, nil
67	
68			case "down", "j":
69				// Navigate down
70				if m.focused < 2 {
71					m.focused++
72				}
73				return m, nil
74	
75			case "left", "h":
76				// Si sur les boutons, aller vers Yes
77				if m.focused == 2 {
78					m.focused = 1
79				}
80				return m, nil
81	
82			case "right", "l":
83				// Si sur les boutons, aller vers No
84				if m.focused == 1 {
85					m.focused = 2
86				}
87				return m, nil
88	
89			case "tab":
90				// Cycle through: checkbox -> Yes -> No -> checkbox
91				m.focused = (m.focused + 1) % 3
92				return m, nil
93	
94			case "shift+tab":
95				// Cycle backwards
96				m.focused = (m.focused + 2) % 3
97				return m, nil
98	
99			case " ":
100				// Toggle checkbox si focus dessus, sinon confirmer la sélection
101				if m.focused == 0 {
102					m.permanentlyRemove = !m.permanentlyRemove
103					return m, nil
104				}
105				return m.handleConfirm()
106	
107			case "enter":
108				return m.handleConfirm()
109

111				// Raccourci pour Yes

114				}
115	
116			case "n", "N", "esc":
117				// Raccourci pour No
118				return m, func() tea.Msg {
119					return DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg{}
120				}
121			}
122		}
123	
124		return m, nil
125	}

127	// handleConfirm gère la confirmation selon l'élément sélectionné
128	func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) handleConfirm() (*DeleteConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
129		switch m.focused {
130		case 0:
131			// Toggle checkbox
132			m.permanentlyRemove = !m.permanentlyRemove
133			return m, nil
134		case 1:

136			return m, func() tea.Msg {
137				return DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg{PermanentlyRemove: m.permanentlyRemove}
138			}

141			return m, func() tea.Msg {
142				return DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg{}
143			}
144		}
145		return m, nil
146	}

236	func (m *Model) getSelectedComponentIndex() int {
237		cursor := m.getCurrentTable().Cursor()

239		if m.activeTab == TabMonitors {

241			var monitors []status.ComponentStatus
242			for _, comp := range m.components {
243				if comp.Type != "ssl" {

245				}
246			}

248			if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(sorted) {

250			}
251			selected := sorted[cursor]
252			// Find matching config component by name+type+target
253			for i, c := range m.config.Status.Components {
254				if c.Name == selected.Name && string(c.Type) == string(selected.Type) && c.Target == selected.Target {
255					return i
256				}
257			}
258		} else {
259			// SSL table - no sorting applied, count through SSL monitors
260			sslCount := 0
261			for i, comp := range m.components {
262				if comp.Type != "ssl" {
263					continue
264				}
265				if sslCount == cursor {
266					// Find matching config component
267					for j, c := range m.config.Status.Components {
268						if c.Name == comp.Name && string(c.Type) == string(comp.Type) && c.Target == comp.Target {
269							return j
270						}
271					}
272					return i
273				}
274				sslCount++
275			}
276		}
277	
278		return -1

479	// cycleSort cycles through sort options: each column asc then desc, then next column
480	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
481		if m.sortAsc {
482			m.sortAsc = false
483		} else {
484			m.sortAsc = true
485			nextIdx := 0
486			for i, col := range sortableColumns {
487				if col == m.sortColumn {
488					nextIdx = (i + 1) % len(sortableColumns)
489					break
490				}
491			}
492			m.sortColumn = sortableColumns[nextIdx]
493		}
494		m.updateTable()
495		return m, nil
496	}

498	// sortedMonitors returns monitor components sorted by the current sort column
499	func (m *Model) sortedMonitors(components []status.ComponentStatus) []status.ComponentStatus {
500		sorted := make([]status.ComponentStatus, len(components))
501		copy(sorted, components)
502	
503		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
504			a, b := sorted[i], sorted[j]
505	
506			var less bool
507			switch m.sortColumn {
508			case sortByTarget:
509				less = strings.ToLower(a.Target) < strings.ToLower(b.Target)
510			case sortByType:
511				less = strings.ToLower(string(a.Type)) < strings.ToLower(string(b.Type))
512			case sortByResponse:
513				less = a.ResponseTime < b.ResponseTime
514			default: // sortByName
515				less = strings.ToLower(a.Name) < strings.ToLower(b.Name)
516			}
517	
518			if m.sortAsc {
519				return less
520			}
521			return !less
522		})
523	
524		return sorted
525	}

Phase 2 démarrée — premier paquet livré : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/12 (CI verte, `test-race` inclus).

| Paquet | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/status` | 0 % | **93,9 %** |
| `internal/ui/status/components` | 0 % | **93,2 %** |
| global | 18,2 % | **22,7 %** |

**Pas de seam nécessaire.** Les constructeurs sont purs et `Update()` est une fonction pure, donc alimenter des messages synthétiques suffit. Aucun test n'exécute une `Cmd` retournée par `Update` — `checkComponents` sort sur le réseau, `tickCmd` dort une seconde ; les assertions portent sur l'état du modèle. Les deux chemins qui touchent le disque (`config.Load` après une sauvegarde, `config.Save`) redirigent `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` vers un dossier temporaire, comme `internal/credentials` — rien n'atteint ton `~/.devdesk`.

Couvert : cycle de check (dont un échec qui ne doit **pas** vider la table), planification des ticks, contrôles de refresh et clamps d'intervalle, navigation, cycle de tri et ses en-têtes ▲/▼, CRUD via formulaire et modale, résultats save/delete avec un reload qui échoue, la filter bar (Rule 136), le routage clavier sous overlay, et le contrat footer Rule 124 — le nombre de lignes de `RenderFooter` est vérifié contre `GetFooterHeight` dans cinq états.

**Deux trouvailles :**
- *Corrigé ici* — l'aide annonçait `n` pour « Add a new monitor » alors que le binding est `ctrl+n` depuis la Rule 111, et `/` n'était pas documenté du tout ; le message d'état vide disait aussi « Press [n] ». Un test vérifie désormais que chaque touche de `GetShortcuts()` figure dans l'aide, pour que les deux ne redivergent pas en silence.
- *Enregistré en D8* — `Model.creating` / `editing` / `confirming` sont écrits à cinq endroits et lus nulle part, et le `case ComponentFormCancelledMsg` est inatteignable (`esc` ferme le formulaire en retournant nil, sans message). Pas corrigé ici : les tests s'appuient volontairement sur `componentForm`/`confirmModal`, donc supprimer ces champs ne cassera rien.

Reste en phase 2 : `containers` (~1 035 lignes), `dashboard` (~920), `gitlab/auth` (~680).

Tu veux que j'enchaîne sur ces trois — et si oui, je repars de `main` une fois #12 mergée, ou j'empile une branche par-dessus ?
enchaine, est-ce qu'il faut repasser par main à chaque fois ou on peut tout faire dans la même branche

Réponse courte : pas besoin d'une branche par paquet. Les trois restants sont indépendants (fichiers disjoints, tests seuls, aucun conflit possible), donc je fais **une seule branche avec un commit par paquet, une PR**. Repasser par `main` n'a d'intérêt que quand un changement dépend du précédent — ici non. Je merge #12 (CI verte) pour repartir propre, puis j'enchaîne.

368	// openExternalPager launches docker logs in the system pager (fallback for power users)
369	func (m Model) openExternalPager() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
370		if !docker.IsContainerID(m.logsContainerID) {
371			log.Printf("ERROR [containers] pager: rejected malformed container ID %q", m.logsContainerID)
372			m.errorMsg = "Cannot open pager — invalid container ID"
373			return m, nil
374		}
375	
376		var pagerCmd *exec.Cmd
377		switch runtime.GOOS {
378		case "windows":
379			// Write to a temp file then open with `more` (always available on Windows; less is not)
380			script := fmt.Sprintf(`docker logs --tail 500 %s > "%%TEMP%%\devdesk-logs.txt" 2>&1 && more "%%TEMP%%\devdesk-logs.txt"`, m.logsContainerID)
381			pagerCmd = exec.Command("cmd", "/c", script)
382		default:
383			pagerCmd = exec.Command("sh", "-c", fmt.Sprintf("docker logs --tail 500 %s 2>&1 | ${PAGER:-less} -R", m.logsContainerID))
384		}
385		return m, tea.ExecProcess(pagerCmd, func(err error) tea.Msg {
386			return PagerExitMsg{Err: err}
387		})

390	// handleContainerLogsLoaded processes fetched log content into the logs viewport
391	func (m Model) handleContainerLogsLoaded(msg ContainerLogsLoadedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
392		m.logsLoading = false
393		if msg.Err != nil {
394			log.Printf("ERROR [containers] logs %s: %v", m.logsContainerName, msg.Err)
395			m.logsRawContent = "Failed to load logs — check logs"
396			m.logsViewport.SetContent(m.logsRawContent)
397			return m, nil
398		}
399		// Strip ANSI escape sequences (colors, cursor moves, etc.) then normalize
400		// line endings. Both are needed: systemd emits colored output, and some
401		// containers use \r for progress-bar overwrites — both break the viewport.
402		content := ansi.Strip(msg.Content)
403		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r\n", "\n")
404		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r", "")
405		m.logsRawContent = content
406	
407		m.refreshLogsViewport()
408		m.logsViewport.GotoBottom()
409		return m, nil
410	}

412	// refreshLogsViewport rebuilds the viewport content applying wrap if enabled.
413	func (m *Model) refreshLogsViewport() {
414		if m.logsWrapEnabled {
415			m.logsViewport.SetContent(wrapLines(m.logsRawContent, m.logsViewport.Width))
416			return
417		}
418		m.logsViewport.SetContent(m.logsRawContent)
419	}
420	
421	// wrapLines soft-wraps content so no line exceeds width runes.
422	func wrapLines(content string, width int) string {
423		if width <= 0 {
424			return content
425		}
426		lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
427		out := make([]string, 0, len(lines))
428		for _, line := range lines {
429			runes := []rune(line)
430			if len(runes) <= width {
431				out = append(out, line)
432				continue
433			}
434			for len(runes) > width {
435				out = append(out, string(runes[:width]))
436				runes = runes[width:]
437			}
438			if len(runes) > 0 {
439				out = append(out, string(runes))
440			}
441		}
442		return strings.Join(out, "\n")
443	}

611	// cycleSort cycles through sort options: each column asc then desc, then next column
612	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
613		if m.sortAsc {
614			m.sortAsc = false
615		} else {
616			m.sortAsc = true
617			nextIdx := 0
618			for i, col := range sortableColumns {
619				if col == m.sortColumn {
620					nextIdx = (i + 1) % len(sortableColumns)
621					break
622				}
623			}
624			m.sortColumn = sortableColumns[nextIdx]
625		}
626		m.updateTable()
627		return m, nil
628	}

630	// sortedContainers returns containers sorted by the current sort column
631	func (m *Model) sortedContainers(containers []docker.Container) []docker.Container {
632		sorted := make([]docker.Container, len(containers))
633		copy(sorted, containers)
634	
635		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
636			a, b := sorted[i], sorted[j]
637	
638			var less bool
639			switch m.sortColumn {
640			case sortByImage:
641				less = strings.ToLower(a.Image) < strings.ToLower(b.Image)
642			case sortByCPU:
643				less = a.CPUPercent < b.CPUPercent
644			case sortByMem:
645				less = a.MemPercent < b.MemPercent
646			case sortByNetRX:
647				less = a.NetRX < b.NetRX
648			case sortByNetTX:
649				less = a.NetTX < b.NetTX
650			case sortByBlockRX:
651				less = a.BlockRX < b.BlockRX
652			case sortByBlockTX:
653				less = a.BlockTX < b.BlockTX
654			case sortByCreated:
655				less = a.CreatedAt < b.CreatedAt
656			default: // sortByName
657				less = strings.ToLower(a.Name) < strings.ToLower(b.Name)
658			}
659	
660			if m.sortAsc {
661				return less
662			}
663			return !less
664		})
665	
666		return sorted
667	}

669	// formatNetBytes formats bytes into a compact human-readable string (e.g. "1.2kB", "3.4MB")
670	func formatNetBytes(b int64) string {
671		switch {
672		case b >= 1e9:
673			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fGB", float64(b)/1e9)
674		case b >= 1e6:
675			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fMB", float64(b)/1e6)
676		case b >= 1e3:
677			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fkB", float64(b)/1e3)
678		default:
679			return fmt.Sprintf("%dB", b)
680		}
681	}

701	// formatMemUsage parses docker MemUsage "150MiB / 7.776GiB" into compact "150M/8G"
702	func formatMemUsage(memUsage string) string {
703		parts := strings.SplitN(memUsage, "/", 2)
704		if len(parts) != 2 {
705			return memUsage
706		}
707		used := formatMemValue(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
708		total := formatMemValue(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
709		return used + "/" + total
710	}
711	
712	// formatMemValue converts "150MiB" -> "150M", "7.776GiB" -> "8G", "512KiB" -> "512K"
713	func formatMemValue(val string) string {
714		val = strings.TrimSpace(val)
715	
716		// Try each unit suffix
717		for _, suffix := range []struct {
718			docker string
719			short  string
720			isGig  bool
721		}{
722			{"GiB", "G", true},
723			{"MiB", "M", false},
724			{"KiB", "K", false},
725			{"B", "B", false},
726		} {
727			if strings.HasSuffix(val, suffix.docker) {
728				numStr := strings.TrimSuffix(val, suffix.docker)
729				num, err := strconv.ParseFloat(numStr, 64)
730				if err != nil {
731					return val
732				}
733				if suffix.isGig {
734					// Round GiB to nearest integer
735					return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%s", num, suffix.short)
736				}
737				// For MiB/KiB, show integer
738				return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%s", num, suffix.short)
739			}
740		}
741		return val
742	}

744	// relativeTime converts a docker CreatedAt timestamp to a human-readable relative time
745	func relativeTime(createdAt string) string {
746		// Docker format: "2026-02-07 12:14:13 +0100 CET"
747		// Try parsing with timezone name suffix
748		t, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02 15:04:05 -0700 MST", createdAt)
749		if err != nil {
750			// Try without timezone name
751			t, err = time.Parse("2006-01-02 15:04:05 -0700", createdAt)
752			if err != nil {
753				return createdAt
754			}
755		}
756	
757		return theme.TimeAgo(t) // Rule 127
758	}

760	// updateTable rebuilds the table rows from the current container list
761	func (m *Model) updateTable() {
762		sorted := m.sortedContainers(m.filteredContainers())
763		rows := make([]table.Row, 0, len(sorted))
764	
765		for _, c := range sorted {
766			cpuStr := "-"
767			memStr := "-"
768			rxStr := "-"
769			txStr := "-"
770			blkRXStr := "-"
771			blkTXStr := "-"
772	
773			if c.State == "running" {
774				cpuStr = fmt.Sprintf("%.1f%%", c.CPUPercent)
775				memStr = formatMemUsage(c.MemUsage)
776	
777				if c.NetIO != "" {
778					rxStr = formatNetBytes(c.NetRX)
779					txStr = formatNetBytes(c.NetTX)
780				}
781				if c.BlockIO != "" {
782					blkRXStr = formatNetBytes(c.BlockRX)
783					blkTXStr = formatNetBytes(c.BlockTX)
784				}
785			}
786	
787			imageWithState := stateIcon(c.State) + " " + c.Image
788	
789			rows = append(rows, table.Row{
790				c.Name,
791				imageWithState,
792				cpuStr,
793				memStr,
794				rxStr,
795				txStr,

225		case 1:

227			m.tokenInput.Focus()

235	// authenticate lance l'authentification
236	func (m *Model) authenticate() tea.Cmd {
237		url := m.urlInput.Value()
238		token := m.tokenInput.Value()
239	
240		if url == "" || token == "" {
241			m.error = "URL and token are required"
242			return nil
243		}
244	
245		// Copier les données nécessaires AVANT la goroutine (Rule 110)
246		saveToHelper := m.saveOption == SaveToHelper
247		saveToConfig := m.saveOption == SaveToConfig
248		config := m.config
249	
250		// Commande asynchrone
251		return func() tea.Msg {
252			// Créer l'auth
253			auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
254	
255			// Authentifier avec saveToHelper
256			result, err := auth.Authenticate(url, token, saveToHelper)
257			if err != nil {
258				return AuthResultMsg{
259					Client: nil,
260					User:   nil,
261					Error:  err,
262				}
263			}
264	
265			// Préparer la config à sauvegarder (copie, pas modification du modèle!)
266			config.GitLab.URL = url
267			if saveToConfig {
268				config.GitLab.Token = token
269			}
270	
271			// Retourner le message avec les données
272			return AuthResultMsg{
273				Client:       result.Client,
274				User:         result.User,
275				Error:        nil,
276				SaveWarning:  result.SaveWarning,
277				SaveToConfig: saveToConfig,
278				ConfigToSave: config,
279			}
280		}
281	}

284	func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
285		url := m.urlInput.Value()
286		storage := m.storage
287	
288		// Commande asynchrone
289		return func() tea.Msg {
290			// Créer l'auth
291			auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(storage)
292	
293			// Supprimer les credentials du storage
294			_ = auth.Logout(url) // Ignorer l'erreur, on déconnecte quand même
295	
296			// NE PAS modifier m.config ici (Rule 110) - le faire dans Update()
297			// Retourner le message de logout complet
298			return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
299		}
300	}

The view layer needed no seam either, for the reason `internal/ui/testutil`
documents: constructors are pure and `Update()` is a pure function, so feeding
synthetic messages fully determines the resulting state. No test executes a
command Update returns — they shell out to Docker, hit the GitLab API, sleep for
a second or open a browser — so the assertions are on model state instead. The
few places that must touch disk (`config.Load` after a save, `config.Save`)
redirect `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` at a temporary directory, the same trick
`internal/credentials` uses.

Three constraints the phase surfaced, worth knowing before phases 3–5:

- **Colour has to be forced to test styling.** Under `go test` lipgloss detects
  no TTY, falls back to the Ascii profile and strips every escape sequence — so
  any assertion about colour passes whatever the code does. `containers` calls
  `lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor)` for the tests that need it and
  restores it afterwards; that is what makes the Rule 122 check (no escape
  sequences in `table.Row` cells) real rather than vacuous. Verified by styling
  a cell on purpose and watching the test fail. `termenv` moved to a direct
  dependency for this.
- **`bubbles/table` keeps its styles unexported**, so `refreshSelectionStyle` is
  asserted by looking for the error-selection escape sequence in the rendered
  table rather than by reading `Styles()`.
- **`sort.Slice` is not stable**, so fixtures must give every sortable column a
  total order or the expected sequences are ambiguous.

Two handlers are deliberately left uncovered in `containers`: `s` and `S` call
`detectShell`, which runs `docker exec` synchronously *inside* `Update`. The
tests drive those keys only in states that return before reaching it. The same
shape appears in `status.reloadConfigAndCheck`, which calls `config.Load()` from
`Update`. Neither is a Rule 110 violation — nothing mutates the model from a
`Cmd` — but I/O in `Update` blocks the event loop and is untestable without a
seam. Worth a look when phase 5 gets to the router.

content.text:
**Sur la question de branche** : pas besoin de repasser par `main` quand les changements sont indépendants. Là j'ai fait une seule branche, un commit par paquet, une PR — repasser par `main` n'a d'intérêt que si un changement dépend du précédent (ou si tu veux mergerdans un ordre précis).

**Phase 2 terminée** : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/13 (CI verte, `test-race` inclus)

| Paquet | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/containers` | 0 % | **87,2 %** |
| `internal/ui/dashboard` | 0 % | **81,5 %** |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/auth` | 0 % | **94,5 %** |
| **global** | 18,2 % | **30,8 %** |

Avec `status` (#12), les cinq paquets de la phase 2 sont tous au-dessus de 80 %.

**Le point qui m'a fait revenir en arrière** : sous `go test`, lipgloss ne détecte pas de TTY, retombe sur le profil Ascii et supprime toutes les séquences d'échappement. Le test Rule 122 que j'avais écrit en #12 (« pas d'ANSI dans les cellules ») passait donc **quoi que fasse le code**. Il force maintenant `termenv.TrueColor` le temps du test — vérifié en stylant une cellule exprès pour voir l'échec. Ça permet aussi d'attester `refreshSelectionStyle`, puisque `bubbles` garde ses styles non exportés : le test cherche la séquence de sélection « erreur » dans le rendu.

**Deux trouvailles :**
- *Corrigé* — l'aide de containers annonçait `S` (shell en nouvelle fenêtre) sans le documenter, même dérive que `n`/`ctrl+n` sur status. Chaque paquet vérifie désormais que toute touche de `GetShortcuts()` figure dans `GetHelpContent()`.
- *Enregistré en D9* — `containers.New()` laisse `sortAsc` à sa valeur zéro : la liste s'ouvre triée **Z→A**, alors que status s'ouvre A→Z. L'en-tête affiche bien `Name ▼`, donc la vue est honnête, mais personne ne l'a choisi. Épinglé par un test plutôt que corrigé — ça change ce que tu vois à l'ouverture, c'est ton arbitrage (une ligne).

**Non couvert volontairement** : `s`/`S` dans containers appellent `detectShell`, qui lance `docker exec` **synchrone dans `Update`**. Même forme que `config.Load()` dans `status.reloadConfigAndCheck`. Ce n'est pas une violation de la Rule 110 — rien ne mute le modèle depuis un `Cmd` — mais ça bloque la boucle d'événements et il faut un seam pour tester. Noté au backlog pour la phase 5.

Prochaine étape possible : phase 3 (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`, ~2 470 stmts) — mais trois de ces fichiers dépassent 800 lignes, donc c'est là que la tension « tester avant de découper » du backlog devient réelle.

Mergée — `main` est sur `a8c8fee`, arbre propre, suite verte.

**Avant d'enchaîner sur la phase 3, il y a la décision que le backlog signale lui-même.** Les quatre paquets restants sont ceux qui dépassent le plafond de 800 lignes :

| Fichier | Lignes |
|---|---|
| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1977 (le backlog disait 1785 — il a grossi) |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1402 |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1299 |
| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 1114 |

Écrire ~2 470 statements de tests contre ces fichiers avant de les découper fige leur structure — c'est exactement ce que le backlog met en garde. Le précédent `docker` (#6) a été découpé *avant* d'être testé, et c'était le cas facile : 7,3 % de couverture, donc presque rien d'épinglé.

Trois options :

1. **Découper d'abord, tester ensuite** — cohérent avec `docker`, mais refactor à comportement constant avec quasi aucun filet de sécurité sur 5 800 lignes.
2. **Tester d'abord, découper ensuite** — le filet existe pour le découpage, mais les tests seront écrits contre une structure qu'on sait vouloir changer (le coût est surtout dans les helpers de test, pas dans les assertions comportementales).
3. **Par paquet, en alternant** — pour chacun : tests comportementaux de surface (`Update`/`View`, sans toucher aux internes), puis découpe, puis complément de couverture. Plus long, mais chaque paquet garde son filet.

Ma recommandation : **(3), en commençant par `netdiag`** — c'est le plus petit des quatre (1114 lignes, et il a déjà 15,9 % de couverture plus deux fichiers de tests existants), donc c'est le bon endroit pour valider que l'alternance marche avant de l'appliquer à `security` (1977).

Tu veux que je parte là-dessus, ou tu préfères une des deux autres ?
ok pour le 3

21	type digResult struct {
22		status    string // NOERROR, NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, …
23		question  string // e.g. "google.com. A"
24		answers   []dnsRecord
25		queryTime string // e.g. "2 ms"
26		server    string // e.g. "8.8.8.8#53"
27	}

29	var (
30		reDigStatus    = regexp.MustCompile(`status:\s*(\w+)`)
31		reDigQueryTime = regexp.MustCompile(`;;\s*Query time:\s*(\d+)\s*msec`)
32		reDigServer    = regexp.MustCompile(`;;\s*SERVER:\s*(\S+)`)
33		reDigAnswer    = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\S+)\s+(\d+)\s+IN\s+(\w+)\s+(.+)$`)
34		reDigQuestion  = regexp.MustCompile(`^;\s*(\S+)\s+IN\s+(\w+)`)
35	)
36	
37	// parseDNSOutput extracts structured data from raw dig output.
38	func parseDNSOutput(output string) digResult {
39		var res digResult
40		section := ""
41	
42		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(output, "\n") {
43			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
44	
45			// Section detection
46			switch {
47			case strings.Contains(trimmed, ";; QUESTION SECTION:"):
48				section = "question"
49				continue
50			case strings.Contains(trimmed, ";; ANSWER SECTION:"):
51				section = "answer"
52				continue
53			case strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ";;") && strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, "SECTION:"):
54				section = "other"
55				continue
56			}
57	
58			// Global metadata
59			if m := reDigStatus.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil && res.status == "" {
60				res.status = m[1]
61			}
62			if m := reDigQueryTime.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil {
63				res.queryTime = m[1] + " ms"
64			}
65			if m := reDigServer.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil {
66				srv := m[1]
67				if idx := strings.Index(srv, "("); idx > 0 {
68					srv = srv[:idx]
69				}
70				res.server = srv
71			}
72	
73			switch section {
74			case "question":
75				if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ";") && !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ";;") {
76					if m := reDigQuestion.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil {
77						res.question = strings.TrimSuffix(m[1], ".") + "  " + m[2]
78					}
79				}
80			case "answer":
81				if trimmed == "" || strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ";") {
82					continue
83				}
84				if m := reDigAnswer.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil {
85					value := strings.TrimSpace(m[4])
86					value = strings.TrimSuffix(value, ".")
87					res.answers = append(res.answers, dnsRecord{
88						name:  strings.TrimSuffix(m[1], "."),
89						ttl:   m[2],
90						rtype: m[3],
91						value: value,
92					})
93				}
94			}
95		}
96	
97		return res
98	}

input.new_string:
This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.

**The order settled on for phase 3 is: surface tests, then split, then complete
coverage** — per package, so each split has a net under it without the tests
being written against a layout that is about to change. It worked on `netdiag`:
the surface pass reached 58.8 % driving `Update()` and `View()` only, the split
moved five blocks of code with the coverage figure unchanged to the statement,
and the completion pass took it to 86.1 %. The discipline that makes it work is
asserting on behaviour rather than on internals — no test named a file, and the

J'ai mergé #14 puis enchaîné sur `workspaces` — deuxième paquet de la phase 3 : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/15 (CI verte)

| | Couverture | `model.go` |
|---|---|---|
| avant | 0 % | 1299 lignes |
| étape 1 (tests de surface) | **60,3 %** | 1299 |
| étape 2 (découpe) | **60,3 %** | **129** |
| étape 3 (complément) | **81,3 %** | 129 |
| global | 37,7 % → **43,6 %** | |

Même vérification qu'avec netdiag : la découpe ne bouge pas la couverture d'un statement (`git show 946bda9` — déplacement pur, seuls les blocs d'import diffèrent).

**Une technique nouvelle qui vaut d'être reprise** : les commandes qui ne touchent qu'au système de fichiers (`createWorkspace`, `deleteEntry`, `renameEntry`, `loadEntries`, `enrichEntry`) sont **exécutées** contre `t.TempDir()` plutôt qu'assertées sur leur identité. `enrichEntry` tourne contre un vrai dépôt git jetable — c'est ce qui prouve que la branche, le remote et les compteurs de l'arbre sale sont bien lus ; un stub ne prouverait que le stub. Skip si `git` n'est pas sur le `PATH`, comme `internal/gitlab`.

**Deux trouvailles, corrigées :**
- **Curseur bloqué** — `bubbles/table.SetRows` ne clampe pas le curseur quand le nombre de lignes diminue. En descendant dans un dossier plus petit (ou en resserrant le filtre), le curseur restait au-delà de la fin : plus rien de surligné, et `enter`, `ctrl+d`, `r`, `ctrl+s` ne faisaient plus rien jusqu'à ce que tu presses une flèche. Le paquet containers évitait ça avec un `GotoTop()` après chaque filtre ; workspaces n'avait pas l'équivalent. À vérifier dans `explorer`, qui a la même forme de drill-down.
- **Dérive de l'aide, troisième instance** — `n` et `Enter` documentés là où les bindings sont `ctrl+n` et `enter`, `/` absent, et le même « Press [n] » périmé dans l'état vide. Status (#12) et containers (#13) avaient la même chose. Trois vues d'affilée : je pars du principe qu'`explorer` et `security` l'ont aussi.

Points qui méritent ton œil : le mode sélection (`enter` valide le dossier **parcouru**, pas la ligne surlignée — se tromper scanne le mauvais arbre, donc c'est épinglé dans les deux sens) et les sémantiques de cache Rule 126 (`ctrl+s` purge un dépôt, `A` saute ce qui est déjà en cache, `ctrl+a` purge tout).

Reste en phase 3 : `explorer` (1402) et `security` (1977).

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   The user asked me to work the DevDesk backlog (`docs/backlog.md`) task by task, in French, across several turns:
   - `"regarde le backlog pour la prochaine tâche"` — identify the next task from the backlog.
   - After choosing option 1 of my AskUserQuestion: fix the three self-contained defects D7, D2, D5.
   - `"merge"` — merge the resulting PR.
   - `"on commence la couverture phase 2"` — start phase 2 of the coverage plan (status, containers, dashboard, gitlab/auth).
   - `"merge avant de continuer"` — merge before continuing (established as the working rhythm).
   - `"enchaine, est-ce qu'il faut repasser par main à chaque fois ou on peut tout faire dans la même branche"` — continue, and answer whether each package needs its own branch. I answered: no, independent changes go on one branch with one commit per package.
   - `"ok pour le 3"` — approved **option 3** for phase 3: **per package, surface tests → split → complete coverage**, starting with the smallest package (`netdiag`).
   - `"continue"` — continue phase 3 (this led to `workspaces`).

   Overarching intent: raise test coverage toward the agreed 80 % target, split files over the project's 800-line ceiling without freezing their structure with tests, and record every finding in `docs/backlog.md`.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Go + Bubble Tea (Elm architecture): `Init`/`Update`/`View`, `tea.Cmd`, `tea.Msg`, pointer vs value receivers on `Model`.
   - `internal/ui/testutil` harness: `Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Resize`, `Msg`, `Msgs`, `MsgOf[T]` — builds messages and drains commands, never spins a `tea.Program`.
   - Testing doctrine established here: **never execute a Cmd that shells out** (Docker, network, GitLab API, browser, `tea.Tick`); assert on model state instead. **Do** execute filesystem-only Cmds against `t.TempDir()`.
   - `lipgloss` colour profile: degrades to Ascii without a TTY under `go test`, making colour/ANSI assertions vacuous. Fix: `lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor)` + restore in `t.Cleanup`. Made `termenv` a direct dependency.
   - `bubbles/table` quirks: `Styles()` is unexported; `SetHeight(h)` subtracts the header so `Height()` returns `h-1`; `SetCursor` clamps to `len-1` (so `-1` on empty); **`SetRows` does NOT clamp the cursor when rows shrink**.
   - `sort.Slice` is not stable → fixtures must give every sortable column a total order.
   - Redirecting `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` to `t.TempDir()` to steer `config.Load`/`config.Save` and `os.UserHomeDir()`.
   - Project rules referenced throughout: 110 (no model mutation in a Cmd), 111 (standard keybindings), 114 (help must be kept in sync), 115 (lipgloss background/no JoinHorizontal), 117 (centralised `theme.*` helpers), 122 (plain text only in `table.Row`), 124 (footer height contract), 126 (scan cache semantics), 127 (`theme.TimeAgo`), 128 (footer message + 3 s clear timer), 129 (English US UI/logs), 130 (dynamic shortcuts), 132/135 (strict key assignment), 136 (`components.FilterBar`), 137 (capitalised imperative shortcut descriptions).
   - Git workflow (from CLAUDE.md, **must be preserved**): never push directly to `main` — the Entire mirror rejects it (`[remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)`). Always `git switch -c <branch>` → `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create --base main --head <branch>` → `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`. `origin` = `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk`, `github` = source of truth. Semantic search (`entire search`) is unavailable in the EU region.
   - Toolchain: `mise run fmt` (go fmt only, no goimports), `mise run lint` (golangci-lint, must be 0 issues), `mise run test-race` (needs cgo/a C compiler — **unavailable locally**, runs in CI on ubuntu-latest).

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`docs/backlog.md`** — the source of truth for tasks; updated in every PR. Now records: D4, D8, D9 open; §1.1 Fixed with D1/D2/D3/D5/D6/D7, the credential-isolation fix, five byte-vs-rune sites, three help-drift instances, the stranded cursor; coverage phase table (phase 0/1 done, 2 done, 3 in progress); the over-800-lines table (5 files left); the phase-3 order and its evidence.

   - **`internal/oci/oci.go`** — D7 fix:
     ```go
     func sanitizeArchivePath(name string) (string, error) {
         clean := strings.ReplaceAll(name, `\`, "/")
         // Drop the leading separator *before* cleaning: path.Clean("/../x") returns
         // "/x", which would silently absorb the traversal instead of exposing it.
         clean = path.Clean(strings.TrimLeft(clean, "/"))
         if clean == "" || clean == "." {
             return "", fmt.Errorf("archive contains an entry with an empty path: %q", name)
         }
         if clean == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") {
             return "", fmt.Errorf("archive entry escapes the root: %q", name)
         }
         return clean, nil
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go`** — D2 fix: added `locked bool`, plus
     ```go
     func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) minFocus() int { if m.locked { return 1 }; return 0 }
     func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) cycleFocus(step int) int {
         min := m.minFocus(); span := 3 - min
         return min + ((m.focused-min+step)%span+span)%span
     }
     func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) toggleCheckbox() { if m.locked { return }; m.permanentlyRemove = !m.permanentlyRemove }
     ```
     Rendering dims the checkbox when locked.

   - **`internal/ui/status/view.go`** — help drift fix: `n` → `ctrl+n`, added `/` entry, empty state `Press [ctrl+n]`.
   - **`internal/ui/containers/view.go`** — added the missing `S` help entry.
   - **`internal/ui/workspaces/view.go`** — `n` → `ctrl+n`, `Enter` → `enter`, added `/`, empty state `Press [ctrl+n]`.

   - **`internal/ui/containers/containers_test.go`** — the colour-profile helpers now reused elsewhere:
     ```go
     func withTrueColor(t *testing.T) {
         t.Helper()
         previous := lipgloss.ColorProfile()
         lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor)
         t.Cleanup(func() { lipgloss.SetColorProfile(previous) })
     }
     func ansiPrefix(s string) string {
         if !strings.HasPrefix(s, "\x1b[") { return "" }
         end := strings.Index(s, "m"); if end < 0 { return "" }
         return s[:end+1]
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/ui/netdiag/model.go`** → split into `validation.go` (97), `run.go` (125), `model.go` (172), `view.go` (214), `header.go` (233), `update.go` (314). The fifth byte-slicing fix lives in `view.go` now:
     ```go
     func firstOutputLine(output string, maxLen int) string {
         for line := range strings.SplitSeq(output, "\n") {
             line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
             if line != "" { return theme.TruncateWidth(line, maxLen) }
         }
         return ""
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/ui/workspaces/model.go`** → split into `messages.go` (97), `model.go` (129), `table.go` (130), `entry.go` (188), `actions.go` (357), `update.go` (450). The stranded-cursor fix is in `table.go`'s `updateTableData`:
     ```go
     m.table.SetRows(rows)

     // bubbles does not clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks, so drilling
     // into a smaller directory — or narrowing the filter — would leave it past
     // the end. Nothing is highlighted then, and every action that resolves the
     // selection (enter, ctrl+d, r, ctrl+s) silently does nothing.
     if m.table.Cursor() >= len(rows) {
         m.table.SetCursor(max(len(rows)-1, 0))
     }
     ```

   - New test files created: `internal/oci/oci_test.go` (rewritten pinned tests), `internal/ui/components/{delete_confirm_modal,creation_form}_test.go` (edits), `internal/ui/status/{status,update,view}_test.go`, `internal/ui/status/components/component_form_test.go`, `internal/ui/containers/{containers,update,view}_test.go`, `internal/ui/dashboard/{dashboard,view}_test.go`, `internal/ui/gitlab/auth/{auth,view}_test.go`, `internal/ui/netdiag/{netdiag,model,view,ports_model,topology_model,dns_formatter}_test.go`, `internal/ui/workspaces/{workspaces,model,view,input,entry}_test.go`.

4. **Errors and fixes:**

   - **`path.Clean("/" + s)` absorbed the traversal** — my first D7 implementation could never reject `../../etc/passwd`. Fixed by stripping leading separators *before* cleaning.
   - **`%q` escaping broke an error-message assertion** (backslash case) — compared against `fmt.Sprintf("%q", tc.entry)` instead of the raw string; added the `fmt` import.
   - **`SetCursor(99)` clamps** — my "out of range cursor returns -1" test was impossible; reframed as a table/`m.components` desync plus a "no matching config entry" case.
   - **`config.Load()` returns `Default()` for a missing file** — wrote malformed YAML to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` under a redirected HOME to force a real failure.
   - **`table.SetHeight(1)` yields `Height() == 0`** — reframed the assertion to "never negative".
   - **`ctrl+n` / `z` swallowed by an active search box** — correct behaviour; my tests were wrong. Reframed one into `TestSearchModeSwallowsViewShortcuts`; added an `enter` to confirm the search before pressing `z`.
   - **Vacuous Rule 122 tests** — proved empirically that lipgloss strips all escapes under `go test`, then forced `termenv.TrueColor` and *verified the test now fails* by deliberately styling a cell. Retro-fixed the already-merged status version.
   - **`bubbles/table.Styles()` is unexported** — asserted the selection style through the rendered output's ANSI prefix instead.
   - **`sort.Slice` ties** — fixtures gave every sortable column a total order (two rounds of fixes).
   - **Default sort was descending in containers** — my expectations were wrong; discovered `sortAsc` is left at its zero value. Recorded as D9, pinned by `TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending`, and split the helper into `rawModel` / `loadedModel`.
   - **Broken intermediate commit (netdiag step 1)** — I staged the split `model.go` without the new files, producing a non-compiling tree. Fixed by `git reset --soft HEAD~1`, moving the new files to `/tmp/ndsplit`, `git checkout model.go`, re-applying only the `firstOutputLine` fix, verifying the tree standalone, then restoring the split for step 2. Also moved `TestSubModelsDeclareNoEditMode` out of `view_test.go` into `topology_model_test.go` because it depended on a step-3 helper.
   - **`loadEntries` semantics backwards** — a missing workspaces *root* is created on first run; only a missing *browsed* subdirectory errors. Split into two tests plus a hidden-entries test.
   - **Manual import fixing after splits** — `mise run fmt` runs `go fmt`, not goimports, so each extracted file's import block had to be written by hand and iterated against `go build`.

5. **Problem Solving:**
   - Resolved the backlog's own stated tension ("writing tests before splitting freezes the structure") by proving a three-step order works: the surface pass drives only `Update()`/`View()`, so the split moves code with coverage **identical to the statement** (58.8 % → 58.8 % for netdiag; 60.3 % → 60.3 % for workspaces).
   - Established that the view layer needs no seam: pure constructors + pure `Update()` means synthetic messages fully determine state.
   - Found and fixed six real defects across the work (Zip Slip, unlocked "permanent" checkbox, dead clamp, fifth byte-slicing site, stranded cursor, three help-drift instances) and recorded three more for the user's decision (D4, D8, D9).
   - Noted for phase 5: `detectShell` (containers) and `config.Load()` (status) perform I/O **inside `Update`** — not Rule 110 violations, but they block the event loop and need a seam.

6. **All user messages:**

   - "on commence la couverture phase 2"

8. **Current Work:**

2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 (the byte-vs-rune lot), then D2, D5 and D7, were fixed; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). **D4 is the only one left**, and it is waiting on a decision
16	rather than on work.
17	
18	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
19	
20	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
21	
22	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
23	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
24	
25	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
26	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
27	than a drive-by fix.
28	
29	Note that the surrounding code moved when D2 was fixed: `tab` / `shift+tab` now
30	cycle through `cycleFocus()`, which skips the locked checkbox. Switching to
31	`↑ / ↓` remains a one-line change to the key names.
32	
33	### D8 — Write-only CRUD flags and an unreachable handler in the status view
34	
35	`internal/ui/status/model.go:64-67` and `internal/ui/status/update.go:57-60`
36	
37	`Model.creating`, `Model.editing` and `Model.confirming` are assigned in five
38	places and read in none: the view keys off `componentForm != nil` and
39	`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
40	commented out at `model.go:139`.
41	
42	`ComponentFormCancelledMsg` is never sent either. `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg`
43	answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
44	`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
45	body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
46	would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.
47	
48	Harmless today, but it is state that lies: a reader reasonably assumes those
49	flags mean something. Found while writing the phase 2 tests; the tests
50	deliberately assert on `componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags,
51	so removing them breaks nothing.
52	
53	**Fix:** delete the three fields, the unreachable case and the message type — or
54	give `esc` a message and make the flags load-bearing. Deleting is the smaller
55	change and matches how the view already works.
56	
57	### D9 — The containers list opens sorted Z→A
58	
59	`internal/ui/containers/model.go:140-147`
60	
61	`New()` sets neither `sortColumn` nor `sortAsc`, so both take their zero value:
62	name, *descending*. The status view, which has the same cycle-sort mechanism,
63	sets `sortAsc: true` explicitly. The header does show `Name ▼`, so the view is
64	at least honest about it — but nobody chose it, and it disagrees with the other
65	list view in the application.
66	
67	**Fix:** set `sortAsc: true` in `New()`, one line. Left for a deliberate call
68	because it changes what the user sees on open.
69	`TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending` pins the current behaviour and says so.
70	
71	### 1.1 Fixed
72	
73	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
74	phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.
75	
76	The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
77	the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
78	was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
79	The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`

81	
82	The workspaces view had it too, found in phase 3: `n` and `Enter` documented

87	`GetShortcuts()` advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would

145	gone.

147	A **fifth site** turned up later, during the phase 3 tests: `firstOutputLine` in
148	`internal/ui/netdiag` sliced `line[:maxLen-3]` to fill the Output column of the
149	results table, so any diagnostic whose first line contained a multibyte rune
150	could be cut in half and bleed across the rows below (Rule 122). Now
151	`theme.TruncateWidth`, pinned by `TestFirstOutputLineKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`.
152	Worth grepping for `[:` on strings when the remaining phases land.
153	
154	The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
155	(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
156	`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).
157	
158	One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
159	`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
160	so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
161	theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
162	
163	**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
164	planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.
165	
166	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
167	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
168	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
169	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
170	same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
171	won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
172	after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
173	strips the path before the helper is ever called.
174	
175	**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
176	the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
177	change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
178	`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.
179	
180	Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
181	path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
182	contexts anyway.
183	
184	Two smaller defects went with it:
185	
186	- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
187	  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
188	  hang indefinitely.
189	- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
190	  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
191	  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
192	  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.
193	
194	`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
195	than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
196	`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
197	common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
198	`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
199	`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.

345	was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,

356	**The order settled on for phase 3 is: surface tests, then split, then complete

358	being written against a layout that is about to change. It worked on `netdiag`:

360	moved five blocks of code with the coverage figure unchanged to the statement,
361	and the completion pass took it to 86.1 %. The discipline that makes it work is
362	asserting on behaviour rather than on internals — no test named a file, and the
363	only ones that reach into the model do so for state the view has no other way to
364	expose.

366	### Race detector cannot run locally
367	
368	`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
369	it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
370	concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.
371	
372	**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
373	every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
374	run reported no data race across all 17 packages.
375	
376	That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
377	tests actually execute, and coverage is 43.6 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
378	paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
379	this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.
380	Phase 2 puts the first full view state machine under the detector.
381	
382	Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
383	avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.

429	### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context
430	
431	Support GitHub as well as GitLab, with **exactly one backend active per
432	configuration context**. A context targets one forge; switching forge means
433	switching context.
434	
435	Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
436	not a chosen design.
437	
438	#### What is coupled to GitLab today
439	
440	| Surface | Size |
441	|---|---|
442	| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
443	| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |
444	
445	The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
446	(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
447	rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
448	interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.
449	
450	Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
451	clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
452	and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
453	`shared.GitLabStats`.
454	
455	#### Model mismatches to settle before coding
456	
457	These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
458	promise.
459	
460	- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
461	  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
462	  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
463	  backend declares.
464	- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
465	  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
466	  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
467	  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there. The `locked`
468	  flag added in §1.1 is the hook for that: a GitHub backend would set it and
469	  leave the box out of reach, as the already-scheduled GitLab case does.
470	- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
471	  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
472	  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
473	  limits and semantics.
474	- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
475	  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
476	  applies either way.
477	
478	#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs
479	
480	Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
481	package needs a seam.
482	
483	Arguments for the CLIs:
484	
485	- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
486	  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
487	  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
488	- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
489	  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
490	- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.
491	
492	Arguments against:
493	
494	- **Per-context isolation conflicts with how these tools store auth.** Both keep
495	  global per-host state (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`). DevDesk contexts want
496	  *different tokens for the same host*. Driving `gh auth switch` from the TUI
497	  would mutate the user's global CLI state — the exact mistake avoided in §1.1 by
498	  scoping `credential.useHttpPath` to the invocation. The clean route is
499	  `GH_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` per invocation, but then DevDesk still owns the
500	  tokens and the main benefit is gone.
501	- **Two more hard dependencies.** Today DevDesk needs `git`, and `docker` only
502	  for the features that use it. Requiring `gh` and `glab` for the core forge
503	  feature is a real setup-friction regression.
504	- **Cost per call.** A process spawn per request, against a reused HTTP
505	  connection today. The dashboard alone issues five calls, and the explorer
506	  paginates.
507	- **Testability regresses.** `internal/gitlab` reaches 100 % with no seam,
508	  because the SDK takes a base URL that an `httptest` server can stand in for.
509	  Shelling out would put it back in the position `internal/docker` was in, needing
510	  a manufactured seam — and stubbed CLI output encodes assumptions about the tool
511	  rather than testing against it.
512	
513	**Current recommendation:** keep Go SDKs (go-gitlab, go-github) for the API
514	surface, and use the CLIs only as an *optional* token source — when a context has
515	no token, offer to read one from `gh auth token --hostname <host>` or
516	`glab auth status`. That takes the convenience without the coupling. Recorded as
517	a recommendation, not a decision.
518	
519	#### Sketch of the work
520	
521	1. Define a `forge` abstraction from what the code actually consumes: current
522	   user, namespace tree, create/delete namespace and repository, initial commit,
523	   dashboard counters, clone URL.
524	2. Replace `shared.State.GitLabClient` with that interface. This is the change
525	   the other 65 call sites follow from.
526	3. Generalise `GitLabConfig` into a per-context forge config carrying a
527	   `type: gitlab | github` discriminator, and migrate existing config files.
528	4. Implement the GitLab backend by moving the existing code behind the
529	   interface — behaviour-preserving, and covered by the tests added in #7.
530	5. Implement the GitHub backend.
531	6. Rename the views and commands, keeping `gla` / `gle` as aliases so muscle
532	   memory survives.
533	
534	Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own: they are a refactor of working code with
535	tests already in place, and they are what makes step 5 tractable.
